sections.title: Structure of the Rib Cage
points: The rib cage is made up of 24 individual ribs (12 pairs).
At the back, all ribs are attached to the 12 Thoracic vertebrae.
Sternum: Also called the breastbone. It is a flat bone in the center of the chest that anchors the ribs at the front.
Intercostal Muscles: Muscles found between the ribs that help in breathing.

sections.title: Three Types of Ribs
points: 1. True Ribs: The first 7 pairs. They attach directly to the sternum using cartilage.
2. False Ribs: The next 3 pairs. They attach to the cartilage of the rib above them instead of the sternum.
3. Floating Ribs: The last 2 pairs. They do not attach to anything at the front.

sections.title: Breathing Mechanics
points: Inspiration (Inhaling): Ribs move up and outwards. Chest volume increases, air enters.
Expiration (Exhaling): Ribs move down and inwards. Chest volume decreases, air is pushed out.

sections.text: The rib cage is flexible because of cartilage. If ribs were attached by hard bone at the front, your chest could not expand to let you breathe!

sections.title: Key Functions
points: Provides a surface for Intercostal muscles to attach.
Manufactures Red Blood Cells in its red bone marrow.
